record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.context_brief: Shah curve equidistribution for larger Lie groups
record.original_question: Does Shah's equidistribution result for L=SO(m,1) and G=SO(n,1), m>n, hold for all Lie groups L containing G=SO(n,1)?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 19 (N. Shah). The same result holds for all Lie groups L containing G = SO(n, 1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer and let $G = \mathrm{SO}(n,1)$, viewed as a connected real Lie group acting by left translations on a finite-volume homogeneous space $L/\Gamma$, where $L$ is a connected real Lie group containing $G$ as a closed subgroup and $\Gamma \subset L$ is a lattice. Fix a one-parameter $\mathbb{R}$-diagonalizable subgroup $\{a_t\}_{t \geq 0} \subset G$ whose expanding horospherical subgroup $U^+$ in $G$ is nontrivial, and let $\varphi : I \to U^+$ be a smooth (or analytic) curve defined on a compact interval $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ which is "generic" in the sense that its image is not contained in any proper subvariety arising from a non-trivial intermediate subgroup (so that the corresponding hypothesis used in Shah's theorem for $L = \mathrm{SO}(m,1)$, $m > n$, is satisfied).

For a fixed point $x_0 \in L/\Gamma$, consider the family of probability measures $\mu_t$ on $L/\Gamma$ obtained by pushing forward the normalized Lebesgue measure on $I$ under the map $s \mapsto a_t \varphi(s) x_0$.

Question: Does $\mu_t$ converge, as $t \to \infty$, in the weak-$*$ topology to the unique $G$-invariant probability measure supported on the closure of the $G$-orbit $G x_0$ in $L/\Gamma$, for every connected real Lie group $L$ containing $G = \mathrm{SO}(n,1)$ (and not only for $L = \mathrm{SO}(m,1)$ with $m > n$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been established in several enlarged settings beyond Shah's original $L=\mathrm{SO}(m,1)$ case: Yang (2013/2016) handled expanding curves in $T^1(\mathbb{H}^n)$, and Shi, and later Yang, established equidistribution for actions of products $\mathrm{SO}(n_1,1)\times\cdots\times\mathrm{SO}(n_k,1)$ inside homogeneous spaces (Acta Math. Sinica 2022; arXiv:1706.01051). A 2025 preprint (arXiv:2511.04799) further extends the result for products of $\mathrm{SO}(n,1)$'s. However, no source establishes the result for arbitrary Lie groups $L$ containing $\mathrm{SO}(n,1)$, so the full conjecture appears to remain open.
